newsitem.title: UK: British retailer W H Smith reports first-ever loss.
newsitem.headline: British retailer W H Smith reports first-ever loss.

text.p: W H Smith, one of Britain's top newsagents, on Wednesday reported a full-year pretax loss of 194.7 million pounds ($304 million) after exceptional items, the first loss in its 204-year history.

Smith also said trading in the current year was patchy, with a positive sales trend in books, news, magazines and stationery offset by disappointing sales of music, videos and computer games. ($1=.6415 Pound)
The loss for the 12 months to June 1 came after a major business review, which W H Smith said had created a platform for a significant improvement in performance.

"It is early in the recovery process and it will take some time fully to capture all the benefits, but (we are) confident we have made the right decisions to enable managers to achieve greater success," the group said in a statement.
Exceptional charges of 123 million pounds relating to the strategic review included provisions for redundancies plus fixed asset and stock write-offs.

Profit before taxes and exceptional items fell to 98.8 million pounds in the year from 114.5 million. Turnover rose to 2.83 billion from 2.69 billion and the total dividend was held at at 15.65 pence.
